lessonsIntro: We couldn't confirm surf lessons at Freshwater Bay. It's a reef break for experienced surfers; learners usually head to Compton Bay, just along the coast.

text: Freshwater Bay is a small cove with a rocky reef break. Wightlink describes it as best for experienced surfers, as the waves can be hollow and powerful, particularly at low tide with a north-easterly or south-easterly swell. Space is limited and the line-up fills quickly on good days, so it isn't a place to learn or practise.

If you're a beginner, Compton Bay is a few minutes west and has gently shelving sand with spots like Fields and Hanover Point suited to learners. iSurf, a mobile school based in Sandown, runs coasteering at Freshwater Bay with its sister company and teaches surfing at whichever island beach suits the day. There's parking nearby and a slipway down to the beach.

cards.title: Experienced surfers

cards.label: Best time
cards.title: Low tide on the right swell
cards.text: Wightlink says it's at its punchiest at low tide on NE or SE swells.

cards.label: Watch out for
cards.title: Reef and crowds
cards.text: Shallow rock and a small, quickly crowded take-off zone.

hireIntro: We couldn't confirm surf hire at Freshwater Bay, so bring your own board.

text: Freshwater's reef waves have power, so experienced surfers usually bring a shortboard or a step-up they trust. Reef boots help on the rocks getting in and out. There's no hire at the bay. On small days, or if you're still learning, take a foam board round to Compton Bay instead, where the sandy beach is far more forgiving.

cards.label: Board
cards.title: Shortboard
cards.text: For the hollow reef waves; learners should use a foamie at Compton.

cards.label: Wetsuit
cards.title: Season-dependent
cards.text: We couldn't confirm a sea-temperature source for this stretch of coast. As a general rule on the English Channel, most people wear a 4/3mm in late spring and autumn and a 5/4mm with boots in winter; check with the school or shop before you go.

cards.label: Other craft
cards.title: SUP on flat days
cards.text: Visit Isle of Wight includes Freshwater Bay among its paddleboard spots, for calm days.

shopsIntro: We couldn't confirm a surf shop in Freshwater.
shopsText: Freshwater has a village close to the bay, but we couldn't confirm a currently trading surf shop there or elsewhere in West Wight. iSurf sells branded clothing online but isn't a hardware shop. If you need a board, wetsuit or leash, sort it out on the mainland before you take the ferry.

lessons.q: Can I learn to surf at Freshwater Bay?
lessons.a: It's not a learner spot. It's a rocky reef with powerful waves; Compton Bay nearby is better for beginners.
iSurf is a mobile school that picks the island beach that suits the day, for ages 8 and up.

lessons.q: What else can I do here?
lessons.a: iSurf and its sister company run coasteering at Freshwater Bay.
